pattern.crimePattern: buyer of a flooded plot drowns the broker in a water tank and dumps him in the lake
pattern.notes: Fictional estate on the real, flooded shore of Lake Nakuru. Rising Rift lakes drowning homes and plots is real and widely reported; no real broker, buyer or estate is depicted.

ob.text: Fishermen report a man found floating among drowned fence posts at Ziwani Gardens on the flooded southern shore of Lake Nakuru at 06:40. He is identified as Hezekiah Onsongo (57), a land broker. Recorded as drowning; suspected fall from a boat.

people.name: Hezekiah Onsongo
people.bio: Sold the Ziwani Gardens plots, and kept selling them as the lake rose, promising "it will go back down".

facts.text: Hezekiah Onsongo, land broker, was found floating among drowned fence posts at Ziwani Gardens at 06:40. Recorded as drowning.
No head injury. His left wrist is bare, with a pale band where a watch used to be.
Lake water sample from plot 47: green, soda-alkaline, thick with blue-green algae.
Barack: he and two others were fishing from 04:00; he found the body at 06:40. No boat was out last night.
Rael: last night Hezekiah went to Lanet to tell a buyer there'd be no refund. "He said the man was a mechanic."
Rael inherits the business. "He kept selling. I begged him to stop."
Records, Hezekiah's line: a call with KYALO MWANZIA at 19:40.
Records: Hezekiah's phone on the Lanet mast 20:25–23:05, then Nakuru South (the lake shore) at 23:20, then off.
Plot 47, Ziwani Gardens: sold to Kyalo Mwanzia for KSh 900,000. Pinned to it: 'Refund or I'll see you in court. — K.M.'
Office visitors' book, last week: 'N. Kipkemboi — came to complain. Shouted. Asked to leave.'
Title deeds for Ziwani plots in his briefcase carry the REGISTRAR OF TITLES oval seal, the familiar design, on watermarked paper.
The Ziwani sale agreements are printed: 'Title processing: Mvua Holdings'.
Job card on the customer's pickup: odometer 48,210 km at 08:00 yesterday, 'brakes not yet road-tested'. It now reads 48,248 km.
Garage job book: three years of customers. Hezekiah Onsongo was never one of them.
Map: Kyalo's garage in Lanet to Ziwani Gardens and back is about 38 km.
Lawrence: he left the pickup on Monday for brakes and has been in Gilgil since, without a car. He hasn't driven it.
At the bottom of Kyalo's water tank: a gold watch, strap snapped, engraved "H.O. — 25 years".
The tank holds clear, chlorinated county water. Amani bottles a sample.
Kyalo's chama book: his loan is current. He owes Hezekiah nothing.
Pastor Waithera: Nicodemus led the singing at the all-night prayer from 20:00 to 05:00.
Grace: Rael stayed with her in Nakuru town from 19:00. They watched the news and slept.
Autopsy: drowning confirmed, water in the lungs and airways. No head injury.
Autopsy: bruising on the back of the neck, as if he was held down.
Autopsy: death between 20:30 and 22:30.
Autopsy: lung fluid kept for water chemistry.
Lab: the lung fluid is fresh, slightly chlorinated, with no algae. Lake Nakuru water is strongly alkaline and full of algae. He did not drown in the lake.
Lab: the lung fluid matches the water in Kyalo's tank.
Toxicology: clean.
Kyalo: "I haven't seen him since August. He won't even take my calls."
Kyalo: "I was working late on a pickup's brakes, here, all night."
Kyalo admits Hezekiah came to the garage at about 20:30. He says Hezekiah laughed about the refund and left.
Kyalo: "I took the pickup out to test the brakes. That's all."
Nicodemus: "I was at church all night."
Rael: "I was at my sister's in town."

interrogations.intro: Kyalo wipes his hands on a rag and keeps wiping. "Onsongo? Dead? Then my money is in the lake for good."

proof.concludes: Hezekiah drowned, held by the neck, but the water in his lungs is clean and chlorinated, with no algae. He did not drown in Lake Nakuru. He was drowned somewhere else and put in the lake.

He went to a mechanic in Lanet about a refund. His phone stayed in Lanet until 23:05 and reached the lake shore at 23:20. Kyalo said he hadn't seen him since August; pressed, he admits Hezekiah came to his garage at 20:30.
The customer's pickup was driven 38 km that night on brakes "not yet road-tested": Lanet to Ziwani Gardens and back.

The water in his lungs matches Kyalo's tank, and his watch is at the bottom of it. Kyalo Mwanzia drowned Hezekiah in his water tank and dumped him in the lake, because he had sold him a plot under the lake and refused a refund.

reconstruction.text: Year by year the lake rises over Ziwani Gardens. Hezekiah keeps selling plots, promising it will go back down. Plot 47 goes to a mechanic for KSh 900,000.
19:40. A phone call: a meeting at the garage "to discuss a refund". At 20:30 Hezekiah arrives in Lanet to say there won't be one.
In the yard he laughs about the lake. Kyalo forces his head into the open water tank and holds it there. The watch strap snaps.
23:00. Kyalo loads him into a customer's pickup and drives to the drowned estate. He leaves him among the fence posts of plot 47.
The pickup is back on its blocks by 00:30, with 38 more kilometres on it than the job card says.

clockPlan.note: No detention needed. Both water tests take 10 h; the case can be charged as soon as the second result is in.

ui.beatNotes: Comparing three samples at once (lung fluid, lake, tank) in the lab view: three test tubes, three readings, one mismatch, one match. Dr. Chebii on the first result: "Your man drowned in drinking water, Detective. Somebody has a very clean tank."
